newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubin says not concerned about recent dollar rise.
newsitem.headline: Rubin says not concerned about recent dollar rise.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said he was not concerned about the dollar's recent rise.

Asked in a taped interview with CNN television, monitored in Tokyo on Tuesday, whether he shared the concern among corporations and on Wall Street that the dollar had risen too high, Rubin said: "No".
He said a strong dollar should help bring low interest rates and low inflation.

"The exchange rate of the dollar is our terms of trade with the rest of the world. And if we have a strong dollar, it will reduce inflation and reduce interest rates. A weak dollar will have the opposite effect," Rubin said.
The United States is competitive across a broad array of industries and that is attributed to management and workers with a good economic policy, he said.
